title: Lisa Su Welcomes Micro Center Austin With AMD Picks
summary: AMD CEO Lisa Su congratulates Micro Center on its Austin store opening, recommending Ryzen processors and Radeon graphics cards for tech enthusiasts.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- AMD CEO Lisa Su congratulated Micro Center on its Austin store opening November 13, 2026, with product recommendations.
- Su specifically highlighted AMD's Ryzen processors and Radeon graphics cards as top picks for the new location.
- The Austin opening expands Micro Center's footprint in Texas, targeting PC enthusiasts and builders in the region.


AMD CEO Lisa Su publicly welcomed Micro Center's new Austin location with a congratulatory message that doubled as a product endorsement. The retail store officially opened its doors November 13, 2026, marking the chain's latest expansion in Texas. Su's recommendation centered on AMD's Ryzen processors and Radeon graphics cards, positioning them as essential purchases for tech enthusiasts visiting the new location.


## Strategic Endorsement for Retail Partner


Su's welcome message arrived via social media shortly after Micro Center announced the Austin opening. The CEO specifically called out AMD's Ryzen processor lineup and Radeon graphics cards as must-have components for PC builders and gamers shopping at the new store. This public endorsement reflects AMD's ongoing partnership with Micro Center, one of the few remaining brick-and-mortar retailers specializing in PC components and DIY computer hardware.


The timing aligns with AMD's aggressive push into consumer markets, where Ryzen CPUs have captured significant market share from Intel in recent years. Radeon graphics cards, while facing stiff competition from Nvidia, remain popular among budget-conscious builders and those seeking alternatives to the dominant GPU maker.


## Micro Center's Austin Expansion


The Austin store represents Micro Center's continued investment in physical retail at a time when many electronics chains have shuttered locations. Austin's tech-savvy population and thriving startup ecosystem make it a natural fit for the retailer's focus on enthusiast-grade hardware and components. The location joins other Texas stores in Houston and Dallas, creating a regional network for PC builders and IT professionals across the state.


Micro Center stores typically stock extensive inventories of processors, graphics cards, motherboards, and peripherals, often at competitive prices compared to online retailers. The chain has built loyalty among DIY computer builders through in-store technical support, build services, and frequent promotions on high-demand components.


## AMD's Retail Strategy


Su's public product recommendations underscore AMD's emphasis on retail partnerships as distribution channels for consumer products. Unlike enterprise AI chips that move through direct sales or cloud providers, consumer CPUs and GPUs rely heavily on retail presence. Micro Center's knowledgeable staff and hands-on shopping experience provide advantages for AMD products that require explanation of technical specifications and performance benefits.


The Ryzen processor family spans budget to high-end desktop segments, offering multi-core performance competitive with Intel's latest chips. Radeon graphics cards target gamers and content creators, with recent generations emphasizing ray tracing capabilities and competitive pricing against Nvidia's RTX lineup.


## Release Date


Officially launched on November 13, 2026, the Micro Center Austin store opened to customers seeking PC components and electronics. Su's congratulatory message arrived the same day, leveraging the store opening to promote AMD products to Austin's tech community.


## What This Means


Lisa Su's public welcome to Micro Center Austin demonstrates how tech CEOs use retail partnerships for grassroots marketing. By personally endorsing AMD products at a store opening, Su connects corporate strategy to individual consumer purchases, reinforcing brand loyalty among enthusiasts who often influence broader buying decisions. For Micro Center, the CEO endorsement validates its relevance in an era of online shopping dominance, while Austin's tech workforce gains another local source for DIY computer hardware.
